title: [FUTURE] Templates + Instances content architecture
description:
Implement Templates + Instances architecture where:
- **Templates** (YAML) define the vocabulary - what kinds of things CAN exist
- **Instances** (Database) define the content - what things DO exist

This includes our own Monastery Arc content, validating the builder workflow end-to-end.

**Full Proposal**: `docs/proposals/builder-content-layer.md`

**Key Design Decisions**:
- Templates are YAML, immutable at runtime, deployed with code
- Instances are DB, live-editable via World Builder UI
- Seeding system populates DB on first boot from YAML seeds
- Nightly export creates git-trackable backups
- Audit trail (not git-style versioning) with rollback support

Inspired by Evennia's prototype system, Unity Prefabs, Unreal Blueprints.
design:
## Architecture

```
Templates (YAML)     →  priv/world/templates/
Instances (Database) →  typed_objects table
Seeds (YAML)         →  priv/seeds/instances/
```

## Implementation Phases

1. **Foundation** - Dual-source loader, is_template field
2. **Database Storage** - Seeder, instance loading, registry indexes
3. **Versioning & Permissions** - Audit trail, rollback, role-based access
4. **World Builder UI** - Templates vs instances, clone workflow
5. **Export & Live Ops** - Nightly export, disable/enable, telemetry
6. **Migration** - Convert existing content, documentation

See `docs/proposals/builder-content-layer.md` for:
- 10 edge cases with handling strategies
- Comprehensive test specifications
- Beads breakdown (~40 tasks)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Templates load from priv/world/templates/
- [ ] Instances load from database
- [ ] Fresh deploy seeds from priv/seeds/instances/
- [ ] World Builder UI shows templates (read-only) vs instances (editable)
- [ ] Clone workflow creates instances from templates
- [ ] Version history with rollback for instances
- [ ] Nightly export to YAML with optional git commit
- [ ] LiveOps disable/enable for instances
- [ ] Monastery Arc content migrated to seeds
- [ ] 10k instance performance test passes
